title: Chronology & periodisation
examples: How do I know if I should use BCE or CE?
What is the difference between a century and a year?
Can you give me an example of a periodisation?

explain.say: Today we are learning how to put events in order.

items: Putting events in order is chronology.
It helps us understand cause and effect.

explain.say: We use BCE and CE to mark time before and after Christ.
Remember that BCE means Before Common Era time.
A century is a period of one hundred years.
For example, the 21st century runs from the year 2001 to 2100.
In everyday life, we use chronology when planning a project.

faq.q: What is the difference between BCE and CE?
faq.a: BCE stands for Before Common Era, and CE stands for Common Era. BCE dates count backwards towards zero, while CE dates count forwards from zero.
asks: How do I know when to use CE instead of BCE?

faq.q: How do I calculate which century a year belongs to?
faq.a: To find the century, you divide the year by one hundred and round up. For instance, the year 1789 is in the 18th century.
asks: What is the rule for centuries?
If the year ends in '00', what century is it?

faq.q: Is there a specific periodisation for history?
faq.a: History is often broken into periods like Ancient, Medieval, and Modern. These are general groupings historians use to study changes over time.
asks: What are the main historical periods?
Does every historian use the same period names?

faq.q: Does the year zero exist in this system?
faq.a: Historically, the transition point is marked, but the counting system moves directly from one side to the other, passing through the year one.
asks: How do I cross from BCE to CE?

faq.q: Can I use a timeline for anything other than history?
faq.a: Yes, you can use timelines for anything that happens in sequence, like steps in a recipe or stages of a process.
asks: Is a timeline only for dates?
Can I use this skill for science?

facts: BCE dates count down towards the year one.
CE dates count up from the year one.
A century covers exactly one hundred years.
The 1st century CE covers the years 1 to 100.

quiz.say: The year 500 BCE is chronologically before which of these dates?
quiz.why: BCE dates are before the Common Era, so any date in CE must come after 500 BCE.

wrong.0: This is wrong because 50 BCE is chronologically after 500 BCE.
wrong.2: This is wrong because 500 CE is much later than 500 BCE.
wrong.3: This is wrong because 100 BCE is closer to 500 BCE, but still before it.

quiz.say: What century does the year 1600 fall into?
quiz.why: We divide 1600 by one hundred, which gives sixteen, so it is the 16th century.

wrong.0: This is wrong because the 15th century ends in the year 1499.
wrong.1: This is wrong because centuries are named using Roman numerals, not just the number.
wrong.2: This is wrong because the 17th century starts in the year 1601.
